html:
Jazz is a music born in the African American communities of New Orleans in the late 1800s and early 1900s. It became one of the great musical forms of the 20th century and spread around the world.

New Orleans was a port city where African, Caribbean, French, Spanish and American traditions met. Jazz drew on blues, ragtime, spirituals, brass band marches and dance music. Its hallmarks are swing, "blue" notes, call and response and, above all, improvisation: players invent melodies on the spot around a shared tune.

Its story moves quickly:

  • New Orleans jazz in the 1910s, with group improvisation.
  • The Jazz Age of the 1920s, when the Great Migration carried Black musicians to Chicago and New York and records and radio spread the music. Louis Armstrong made the soloist the star.
  • Swing in the 1930s, the big bands of Duke Ellington and Count Basie, America's popular dance music.
  • Bebop in the 1940s, faster and harder, led by Charlie Parker and Dizzy Gillespie.
  • Cool, modal and free jazz after 1950, from Miles Davis to John Coltrane.

Jazz grew up under segregation, and its Black musicians often played to white audiences they could not sit beside. It was tied to the Harlem Renaissance, and it fed rock and roll, soul and hip hop. The US government even sent jazz musicians abroad in the Cold War as a sign of American freedom. Today it is played and studied around the world.
sum: Jazz is a music born in the African American communities of New Orleans in the late 1800s and early 1900s. It became one of the great musical forms of the 20th century and spread around the world.
